Omega Seamaster 300M Quartz "Bond" – Red Writing | Swiss Quartz | All Original

The Iconic Bond Seamaster with the Classic Red Script Dial.

The Omega Seamaster 300M Quartz "Red Writing" is one of the most recognizable dive watches of the modern era. Produced in the early 2000s, this model features the famous red "Seamaster" script on the wave-pattern dial—a detail highly appreciated by enthusiasts of the classic 300M generation.

Made famous through its association with James Bond, the Seamaster 300M blends professional diving capability with timeless Swiss craftsmanship, making it one of Omega's most enduring and collectible sports watches.

SPECIFICATIONS
Model: Omega Seamaster 300M Quartz "Red Writing"
Era: Early 2000s
Movement: Original Omega Swiss Quartz Movement, fully tested and running accurately.
Case Size: 41 mm (excluding the crown).
Crystal: Sapphire Crystal.

CONDITION
All Original.

Sapphire crystal is clear and in excellent condition.
Stainless steel case and bracelet show scratches from normal wear. Please examine the photos carefully for cosmetic details.
Original Swiss quartz movement is running accurately and functions perfectly.
Original bracelet is in good condition and ready to wear.

COLLECTOR'S NOTE
The Seamaster 300M became an instant icon after its debut in the 1990s and achieved legendary status through its appearance on the wrist of James Bond beginning with Golden Eye. The early-generation models featuring the red "Seamaster" lettering are especially beloved by collectors for their classic aesthetics and unmistakable identity.

Powered by Omega's reliable Swiss quartz movement, this version offers exceptional accuracy, low maintenance, and the slim wearing profile that many enthusiasts prefer. Original examples from the early 2000s continue to be sought after as modern classics within the Omega collection.

Carefully inspected to verify the originality of its key components and the proper operation of its movement, this watch is an excellent opportunity to own one of the most iconic Swiss dive watches ever produced.

TERMS OF SALE
This is a pre-owned watch and may show signs of age and use consistent with its condition.

Please review all photos, videos, and the description carefully before purchasing, as they form an important part of the listing. If you have any questions or would like additional photos or information, please feel free to send me a message. I'll be happy to assist.

listing.title: Omega Seamaster Ref. 2635 “Hammer” Automatic, Swiss 1952
listing.body:
Rare, Beautiful and Iconic ** Early Vintage Omega Seamaster Ref. 2635 “Hammer” Automatic, Swiss 1952 **

Launched in 1948 to concur with Omega’s Centennial celebrations, the Seamaster line issued as a civilian version inspired by the waterproof wristwatches Omega had produced for the British military in the latter part of WWII. The new design concept was: “A robust yet elegant watch for active individuals who want a watch for “town, sea and country”.

All the early Seamaster watches were equipped with self-winding movements, and rapidly found favor in the marketplace for their robustness, accuracy and reliability. 

Moreover, in those days water-resistant watches generally had lead or shellac gaskets to hermetically seal the watch case… and these were susceptible leakage resulting from temperature changes… the Seamaster watchcase was sealed with a rubber O-ring gasket of the type that had proven its abilities in submarines during the Second World War. Thus, in 1955 the Seamaster achieved its first diving-record, when Australian Gordon McLean wore one to the depth of 62.5 meters.

Additionally, the Seamaster was independently tested by the Swiss Laboratory for Watch Research which subjected 50 cases to tests at a simulated depth of 60 meters. After temperature changes of -40° C to 50° C in quick succession, the cases showed no sign of water infiltration. In fact, the engineers at OMEGA were so confident of the Seamaster that one flew the Polar Route over the North Atlantic in 1956… attached to the outside of a Douglas DC6 aircraft!

The Omega Seamaster also is Iconic for its role as the trusted watch of 007 agent James Bond… Of which the Semaster Ref. 2635, presently offered here for your consideration, is the venerable grandfather! 

Material: Stainless Steel 
Dial: Silvered with Applied Numerals and Shark -Tooth Batons, Fully Original
Bracelet: Black Crocodile 
Buckle: Omega, Stainless steel 
Movement: Omega Calibre 354, “Hammer” Automatic Self-Winding 
Case: 32.5 mm diameter (excluding the winder crown) x 40 mm Length (lug-to-lug)
Condition: Excellent, Fully Serviced by Master Swiss Watchmaker.

Shipping: Worldwide; Duty-Free Shipping within Europe




OMEGA Watch Company
The Omega Watch Company was founded by Louis Brandt in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, in 1848. Initially the firm assembled key-wound precision pocket watches using parts supplied by local craftsmen. 

After Louis Brandt's death in 1879, his two sons Louis-Paul and Cesar took over control of the business. Louis-Paul and César Brandt both died in 1903, leaving one of Switzerland's largest watch companies - with an annual production of 240,000 watches and 800 employees - in the hands of four young Brandt family members, the oldest of whom was Paul-Emile Brandt. 

The difficult economic times that followed World War I caused Paul-Emil Brandt, as of 1925, to actively seek a union between OMEGA and Tissot… then subsequently their merger in 1930 within the group SSIH. 

By the 1970s, SSIH had become Switzerland's no 1 producer of finished watches; however, due to the severe monetary crisis and recession of 1975 through 1980, in 1981 SSIH had to be bailed out by the banks.. so that in 1985 the holding company was taken over by a group of private investors and renamed SMH, Societe suisse de microelectronique et d'horlogerie.

The new group achieved rapid growth and success to become today's top watch producer in the world. Named Swatch Group in 1998, it now notably includes Blancpain and Breguet. 

Dynamic and flourishing, OMEGA remains one of its most prestigious flagship brands.

listing.title: Vintage Omega Constellation Swiss Watch, Ref. 2782-3 SC, Bumper Automatic Cal. 354, Crosshair Dial from 1954
listing.body:
The Constellation was Omega's answer to the question of how accurate a series-produced wristwatch could be. Launched in 1952, every example carried official chronometer certification, and this Ref. 2782 from 1954 belongs to the first generation - the last Constellation reference powered by a bumper automatic before Omega moved to full-rotor winding. For collectors of early Constellations, the 2782 is where the story begins.

The 35mm stainless steel case wears cleanly at 42mm lug to lug, with the gold observatory medallion set into the screw-down case back - the emblem commemorating Omega's observatory trial victories that gave the model its name. The crosshair dial is the quiet star here: silvered white, quartered by fine black lines, with applied gold Arabic numerals at 12, 3, 6, and 9 between faceted arrowhead markers. Gold dauphine hands and the small gold star above the Constellation script complete a dial layout that collectors seek out specifically in this configuration. The watch comes on a steel mesh bracelet, a later fitting that suits its character.

Inside is the Caliber 354, the chronometer version of Omega's bumper automatic family: 17 jewels, 19,800 vph, Incabloc shock protection, and a swan-neck micrometer regulator that allowed the fine adjustment demanded by chronometer testing. The pivoting bumper weight winds with the characteristic soft knock that gives these movements their name. Serial number 14035077 dates production to 1954.

Stainless steel case, Ref. 2782-3 SC
Case diameter: 35mm
Lug to lug: 42mm

Screw-down case back with gold observatory medallion
DIAL:

Applied gold Arabic numerals at 12, 3, 6, 9 with faceted arrowhead markers
Gold dauphine hands with central seconds
Gold star above the Constellation signature
MOVEMENT:
Omega Caliber 354, chronometer-rated bumper automatic, 17 jewels
19,800 vph, approx. 40-hour power reserve
Serial number 14035077, dating to 1954
Swiss made

listing.title: The Submarine Commanders' Wristwatch, United Kingdom 1931
listing.body:
Rare and Historical ** The Submarine Commanders' Wristwatch, UK 1931 **

Grandfather of the waterproof wristwatch and Godfather of the now iconic Rolex Oyster Submariner, the Submarine Commanders’ wristwatch led the way for Rolex founder Hans Wilsdorf… and ultimately – on March 31st 1922 (copyright N° 51632) - saw its brand-name become one of Rolex’s! 

In the Midst of World War I, two British Submarine Commanders approached Brook & Son requesting they “Consider the construction of a special watch suitable for their work. As Edinburgh's foremost jewelers, watch and clock makers as well as official Goldsmiths to His Majesty The King… to Her Royal Highness Princess Louise… and to The King's Bodyguard (The Royal Company of Archers), this venerable firm accepted the challenge!

The Submariners explained that the watch must fulfill rigorous conditions, notably be water-tight: “For,- even when a submarine is on the surface, the deck is always more-or-less-awash”…  It must be non-magnetic: “For underwater the submarine is driven by electricity and in such a limited space watches made of magnetic materials are necessarily affected”…. Also for the latter reason, use of a compensation balance of the ordinary kind to regulate the watch’s speed would be impossible: “The balance must be of some material which shows a minimum of expansion and contraction due to temperature variations”!

Brook & Son responded with a very innovative solution: 

In designing their water-tight watch case, they correctly understood that any watch’s Achilles heel was the opening through which protrudes the stem with which a watch is set and wound. So, they incorporated a gland-seal in the stem’s passageway, a design innovation that not long thereafter also was incorporated into the Rolex Oyster water-proof screw-down crown, whose patent Rolex founder, Hans Wilsdorf, purchased from George Perret and Paul Perregaux in 1926.

For the Submarine Wrist Watch’s mechanism, Brook & Son turned to Swiss watch-industry giant Tavannes, noted for their very high quality watch movements as well as other cutting-edge watch-making inventions. Tavannes’ solution for the Submarine Wrist Watch was to develop exclusive iron nickel alloy components which not only were impervious to magnetism but also displayed negligible expansion/contraction due to temperature changes.

The Submarine Wristwatch was so ground-breaking that its creation resulted in a scientific publication about it in “The Horological Journal”, December 1917 (see http://www.vintagewatchstraps.com/waterproof.html).

Manufacturing and development of the Submarine Wrist Watch continued well beyond WWI. In 1931, London jeweler and inventor of the expansion bracelet, E. Harrup (in collaboration with F. Wachter in New York) redesigned the Submarine’s case, integrating further improvements (patent N° 358370 and N° 362229), which notably included the bezel and a water-tight snap-back for the case.

A well-documented fact is Rolex’s decades-long preoccupation with producing a water-proof wristwatch. Notably, as of the 1910s, they successively( as well as simultaneously) employed Denison’s screw-back cases, Borgel’s water-tight watchcases, Baumgartner’s double  hermetic cases, etc. for their Rolex watches)… culminating in Rolex’s 1926 launch of the Oyster watchcase. 

Back then, Rolex and the Submarine Wrist Watch both were British watch companies; and Rolex founder Hans Wilsdorf would have followed the development and evolution of this “water-tight watch” competitor, the Submarine Wrist Watch. This is confirmed by Rolex’s 1922 registration of “The Submarine” brand name. Apparently, it wasn’t previously copyrighted. Notwithstanding, almost a decade onward, Harrup still was commercializing wristwatches called “Submarine”!

Interestingly, although the Submarine Wrist Watch also appears to have played a role in Rolex history, including inspiring the name of Rolex’s current line of Sports Watches (the Rolex Submariner), information about the Submarine Wrist Watch, has largely remained a “well-kept secret”…

Indeed, the author of a research publication about the Submarine Wrist Watch, appearing May/June 2014 in the NAWCC Watch & Clock Bulletin, concludes: 

“The one question that puzzles me is why so little is known about these historically important watches? I have never seen them mentioned in any book or article. They were clearly fully waterproof nearly ten years before the Rolex Oyster, which many people think of as the first waterproof watch, or the first waterproof wristwatch. They were also non-magnetic and temperature compensated, if the article in the H[orological] J[ournal] is correct.

The Submarine watch was also very practical compared to the Oyster - there is no need to unscrew the crown to wind or set the watch, and therefore no threads on the stem tube to wear, the Achilles heel of the early Oysters before automatic winding was introduced, they remain waterproof while both winding and setting the watch, which the Oyster doesn't, and there is no need to remember to screw down the crown after winding, a feature that has caused grief to many Oyster owners over the years. The compressed gasket sealing for the stem is perhaps not as ultimately waterproof as a screw down crown in withstanding water pressure at diving depths, but then again, Rolex didn't make any claims about this for the first Oysters, allowing Omega to make the claim of producing the first dive watch in the 1932 Omega Marine.

I suppose the answer could be found in the way the watch came about, during the depths of WW1 as the result of a request by two submarine commanders. The extra work involved in making the watch waterproof and anti-magnetic would have made it more expensive, and the military involvement could have made it hush-hush. Was it regarded as too expensive to be commercially viable, was it secret, or was it that no one involved saw that the public might want a waterproof watch - 1917 was of course long before recreational diving became popular, or was even possible. The promotion of a waterproof watch as something for the average person to want or need seems to have been a particular vision of Hans Wilsdorf, similar to the way that Steve Jobs had a vision for the iPod and iPad and almost single handedly created markets for portable mp3 players and tablet computers. But without such a visionary to champion its cause this watch faded into obscurity.”

listing.title: Vintage Universal Genève Automatic Watch Cal 138SS 14K Solid Gold Case Sharp & Dohme Dial 1954 Presentation Watch Running
listing.body:
I placed on a time graph and it’s running +- 30 seconds a day 

This elegant mid-century Swiss wristwatch represents a fascinating intersection of fine horology and American pharmaceutical history. Produced by the prestigious Swiss manufacturer Universal Genève, the watch houses the respected Caliber 138SS automatic movement, one of the brand’s early self-winding calibers developed during the golden era of mechanical watchmaking in the late 1940s and 1950s. Universal Genève was widely admired for its refined engineering and reliable in-house movements, and the Caliber 138 series became one of the company’s dependable automatic platforms during the post-war expansion of Swiss wristwatch production.

The watch is housed in a solid 14K gold case manufactured by the Star Watch Case Company of Taunton, Massachusetts, a respected American case maker that produced high-quality gold cases for imported Swiss movements destined for the United States market. With gold prices historically strong, the case itself carries substantial intrinsic value while maintaining the classic understated luxury expected of a mid-century Swiss dress watch.

The dial is marked “Sharp & Dohme – Automatic – Swiss,” referencing the historic American pharmaceutical company Sharp & Dohme. Founded in the 19th century and later merged with Merck & Co., the company frequently commissioned fine Swiss watches as presentation awards for executives and high-performing employees. Watches such as this were commonly given in recognition of professional achievement or years of service.

The back of the case remains engraved with its original presentation inscription:

D.G. CLEMMONS
MEMBER – 1954
ALL AMERICAN SALES TEAM

This engraving firmly dates the watch to the early 1950s and connects the piece to its original owner and the mid-century corporate culture in which presentation watches were symbols of recognition and accomplishment.

The watch is currently fitted with a MOD DEP Swiss-made rubber strap, a comfortable vintage strap style that wears well while helping protect the original gold case.

This example has clearly been cared for over its lifetime and the movement shows signs of past servicing. The watch will run and keep time when manually wound and left resting, and it has been worn throughout the week with reasonable timekeeping. However, when the crown is pulled out to set the time, the hands tend to stick or hesitate during adjustment. Because of this behavior, the watch should be professionally serviced in order to run properly and ensure smooth operation of the time-setting mechanism. As with most mechanical watches from the 1950s, routine servicing is considered normal maintenance and will help preserve the movement for continued use.

Altogether this piece represents a wonderful example of mid-century Swiss watchmaking, combining Universal Genève engineering, a solid 14K gold case, and a unique connection to American pharmaceutical corporate history.

This rubber-clad version gives the classic Cartier Santos silhouette a more contemporary, casual, and masculine feel.

listing.title: Vintage 1961 Omega Constellation Pie Pan 18K Solid Gold Automatic Cal.561 Ref.14393/4 SC 34mm
listing.body:
This watch comes from my personal collection and is being offered for sale because I no longer use it.

A highly collectible vintage Omega Constellation dating from approximately 1960–1961, featuring a solid 18K yellow gold case, a warm gold Pie Pan dial with natural age-related patina, distinctive sculpted lugs and the renowned Omega Caliber 561 automatic chronometer movement.

The rich golden tones and naturally aged dial give this watch a unique vintage character. It is an elegant piece for an Omega collector and also an impressive choice for formal wear or a special gift.

WATCH DETAILS

• Brand: Omega
• Collection: Constellation
• Reference: 14393/4 SC 61
• Approximate production period: 1960–1961
• Movement serial number: Approximately 18,005,709
• Movement: Omega Caliber 561
• Winding: Automatic
• Jewels: 24
• Movement grade: Chronometer
• Functions: Hours, minutes, central seconds and date
• Case material: Solid 18K yellow gold
• Gold hallmark: 18K / 0.750
• Case diameter: Approximately 34–34.5mm, excluding the crown
• Dial: Gold Pie Pan dial with natural age-related patina
• Hour markers: Applied gold baton markers with dark inlays
• Hands: Gold-tone hands with dark inlays
• Date window: Positioned at 3 o’clock
• Crystal: Acrylic crystal with date magnifier
• Crown: Omega-signed gold-tone crown
• Case back: Solid 18K gold screw-back with Omega Constellation observatory medallion
• Strap: Black leather replacement strap

CONDITION

The watch is presented in attractive collector-grade vintage condition.

The solid 18K gold case retains its elegant sculpted profile and distinctive lugs. Visible surface marks, fine scratches and signs of previous wear are present, particularly on the case back, and are consistent with the age of the watch.

The gold dial has developed a warm and attractive natural patina. This aging gives the watch an individual character and has not been concealed or digitally altered in the photographs.

The applied markers, hands, Omega logo, Constellation lettering and star remain visually attractive. The copper-tone Omega Caliber 561 movement is shown clearly in the listing photographs.

Please carefully examine all photographs, as they form an important part of the description. The watch shown is the exact watch the buyer will receive.

VINTAGE WATCH NOTICE

This is a vintage mechanical watch and minor daily time variation may occur depending on position, temperature, power reserve and wearing habits.

Water resistance has not been tested and is not guaranteed. Please keep the watch away from water, moisture, steam and strong magnetic fields.

AUTHENTICITY AND RETURNS

The buyer is welcome to have the watch inspected and authenticated by a qualified watchmaker or vintage Omega specialist after delivery.

Returns are accepted within 21 days from the confirmed delivery date. The watch must be returned in the same condition in which it was received, without damage, alteration, polishing or removal of original components.

Please contact me before purchasing if you require additional photographs, measurements or movement information.

listing.title: Omega Constellation Automatic Cal 1001 Grey Dial Unpolished Original Watch
listing.body:
Omega Constellation Stainless Steel Automatic
Automatic | Grey Dial | Unpolished Case | Cal. 1001 | Circa 1970s

A classic Omega Constellation that embodies everything collectors admire about vintage Swiss watchmaking.

This Omega Constellation Ref. 168.003 represents the golden era of the Constellation collection, combining refined design with one of Omega's dependable automatic movements. Crafted in stainless steel, the watch features an elegant grey dial accented by a practical date window at 3 o'clock, creating a sophisticated look that remains timeless more than fifty years later.

Powering the watch is the respected Omega Caliber 1001 automatic movement, part of Omega's renowned 1000-series family introduced during the 1970s. Appreciated for its reliability, slim architecture, and smooth operation, it remains a favorite among vintage Omega enthusiasts.

One of the most desirable aspects of this example is its honest unpolished condition. The case retains its original factory lines and proportions, preserving the character that serious collectors value. Unlike heavily refinished examples, this watch proudly displays the authentic surfaces and geometry intended by Omega.

Adding further collector appeal, the watch retains its original Omega signed acrylic crystal (signed plexiglass) and original Omega signed crown—important details that confirm its originality and are becoming increasingly difficult to find on vintage Constellation models.

Measuring 34mm in diameter with a 39mm lug-to-lug length, the watch offers classic vintage proportions while maintaining excellent wrist presence. It is fitted with a new premium aftermarket leather strap, giving it a refined appearance ready for daily enjoyment.

Presented in good vintage condition and accompanied by a replacement box, this is an outstanding opportunity to own a highly original Omega Constellation from one of the brand's most celebrated decades.

A true Omega Constellation—where heritage, originality, and timeless Swiss craftsmanship meet.

listing.title: Omega Constellation Tonneau Linen Dial Automatic Cal 712 Unpolished Vintage 1960s Dress Watch
listing.body:
Omega Constellation Tonneau Linen Dial
Automatic | Linen Dial | Cal. 712 | Unpolished | Circa 1960s

An exceptional Omega Constellation that beautifully represents the refined elegance of late 1960s Swiss watchmaking.

This Omega Constellation Ref. 153.014 combines one of Omega's finest ultra-thin automatic movements with a sophisticated tonneau-shaped case, resulting in a dress watch that is both elegant and unmistakably distinctive. Produced during one of Omega's most celebrated eras, this reference remains highly sought after by collectors for its clean design and exceptional craftsmanship.

The highlight of this watch is its beautiful silver linen dial, whose finely textured surface catches the light differently from every angle. Complemented by slim applied baton hour markers, the dial delivers a level of depth and refinement rarely found on conventional sunburst dials. It is a subtle detail that seasoned collectors immediately appreciate.

Powering the watch is the renowned Omega Caliber 712 automatic movement, one of Omega's premium ultra-thin chronometer-family calibers developed during the golden age of the Constellation line. Celebrated for its slim architecture, reliability, and smooth performance, the Cal. 712 remains one of the most desirable vintage Omega movements.

This example is particularly attractive because it remains in unpolished condition, preserving the crisp factory lines and original geometry of the tonneau case. Collectors increasingly value honest, unpolished watches over heavily refinished examples, making this an especially desirable piece.

The watch retains its original Omega signed crown and is fitted with a new premium aftermarket leather strap, providing everyday comfort while maintaining its authentic vintage character.

Measuring 31mm in diameter, 40mm lug-to-lug, and only 8mm thick, the watch wears remarkably well thanks to its elongated tonneau profile and ultra-slim construction.

Presented in good vintage condition and accompanied by a replacement box, this is an increasingly collectible Omega Constellation for enthusiasts who appreciate originality, understated elegance, and exceptional Swiss watchmaking.

listing.title: Vintage Omega Constellation Pie Pan 14K Gold Capped Cal.561 Automatic 34.2mm Dog Leg Lugs
listing.body:
This watch comes from my personal collection and is being offered for sale because I no longer use it.

A collectible vintage Omega Constellation featuring the iconic Pie Pan dial, sharply defined dog-leg lugs, a 14K gold-capped case and the highly regarded Omega Caliber 561 automatic chronometer movement.

The light silver-white dial is complemented by applied gold-tone baton hour markers with black inlays, creating a refined contrast and a timeless 1960s dress-watch appearance.

WATCH DETAILS

• Brand: Omega
• Collection: Constellation
• Approximate period: 1960s
• Movement: Omega Caliber 561
• Winding: Automatic with manual-winding capability
• Jewels: 24
• Movement grade: Chronometer
• Functions: Hours, minutes, central seconds and date
• Case: 14K gold-capped case with stainless-steel back
• Case diameter: Approximately 34.2mm
• Case design: Sharp dog-leg lugs
• Dial: Light silver-white Pie Pan dial
• Hour markers: Applied gold-tone baton markers with black inlays
• Movement finish: Clean copper-tone Omega movement
• Strap: Black leather replacement strap
• Buckle: Aftermarket replacement buckle

CONDITION

The watch is presented in attractive vintage collector condition.

The case retains a sharp profile, with clearly defined dog-leg lugs and an elegant 14K gold-capped finish. Normal signs of age and previous use may be visible upon close inspection.

The light silver-white dial has a clean and elegant appearance. Its applied gold-tone hour markers feature distinctive black inlays, giving the watch a refined two-tone character.

The Omega Caliber 561 automatic chronometer movement appears clean and bright. No recent service history is included unless otherwise stated.

Please examine all listing photographs carefully, as they form an important part of the description. The watch shown in the photographs is the exact watch the buyer will receive.

VINTAGE WATCH NOTICE

This is a vintage mechanical watch, and minor daily time variation should be expected depending on position, temperature, power reserve and wearing habits.

Water resistance has not been tested and is not guaranteed. Please keep the watch away from water, moisture, steam and strong magnetic fields.

AUTHENTICITY AND RETURNS

The buyer is welcome to have the watch inspected and authenticated by a qualified watchmaker or vintage Omega specialist after delivery.

Returns are accepted within 21 days from the confirmed delivery date. The watch must be returned in the same condition in which it was received, without damage, alteration, polishing or removal of components.

Please contact me before purchasing if you require additional photographs, movement details, case-reference information or measurements.

***We greatly appreciate your support of our small business!***
*Buying here is buying direct from an experienced watchmaker, TIM MACKRAIN, who provides care before and after the sale.

Beautiful classic Omega Seamaster men's vintage watch. 34 mm stainless-steel case #14750 1 SC has Seamaster logo and vintage presentation on back. Original finish in silver on original dial has original applied silver baton and dagger hour markers and original silver baton hands. I personally cleaned and oiled this caliber 601, 17 jewel manual wind movement, adjusted 2 positions and it is running strong and keeping time well. Serial number 17974703 dates watch to 1960. This photo is of the actual movement in this watch! New Swiss made optical grade acrylic crystal and original signed Omega crown. New OmegaAddict high-quality black, dark brown or light brown 18 mm comfortable leather strap with SILVER buckle. Please specify your choice of color when you make your purchase. This vintage manual wind Seamaster is serviced and ready to wear! 
*Watch comes in gift box with professional appraisal and ONE YEAR WARRANTY!
*Please read SHIPPING POLICY, RETURN POLICY and WARRANTY TERMS!
*OMEGAADDICT ONE YEAR WARRANTY: Omega mechanical watches were engineered to last generations. These beautiful vintage time pieces are now 45+ years old and perform best with regular maintenance. Because of their excellent reputation, I can offer a one-year warranty; no charge for labor, only charging for parts (if needed) and return shipping ($20 in U.S. /$45 outside U.S.). 
*FREE LIFETIME SERVICE AGREEMENT:  Your watch should be SERVICED every 3 years after date of purchase.  A SERVICE includes - movement dismantled, movement cleaned and oiled, case cleaned and new crystal.  With this agreement, your 3-Year Service will cost $300 plus parts and return shipping (20 in U.S. /45 outside U.S.).

OmegaAddict - Sales and Service of Vintage Omega Watches
For restoration or service of your VINTAGE OMEGA WATCH message Tim Mackrain. Any problems with a watch purchased from me, I will take care of it right away – always have and always will.  I believe in quality not quantity. Every watch I sell gets my full attention to detail.  Authenticity is money back guaranteed on all my watches. I do not sell fake watches!  We are located in sunny Phoenix, Arizona. Feel free to message me with any watch questions from 8am to 5pm - AZ time. 602-795-8894

listing.title: Vintage Omega Constellation Manhattan 18K Gold Day-Date Ref.196.1070 Original
listing.body:
A distinguished example of Omega's iconic Constellation collection, the Constellation Manhattan Ref. 196.1070 embodies the refined elegance that has defined the series since its celebrated redesign in the early 1980s. Crafted entirely in 18K solid yellow gold, this sophisticated timepiece features the unmistakable integrated Manhattan case with its signature bezel "griffes" (claws), a slim profile, and a practical Day-Date display.

Powered by a precise Swiss quartz movement, the watch combines luxurious craftsmanship with exceptional everyday reliability, making it equally appealing to collectors and enthusiasts of classic Omega dress watches.

Technical Specifications

SPECIFICATION:
Brand: Omega
Collection: Constellation Manhattan
Reference: 196.1070
Movement: Swiss Quartz — Working Tested & Curated.
Functions: Hours, Minutes, Central Seconds, Day & Date.
Dial: Original Omega dial with applied hour markers, Day-Date display, and original hands.
Case Material: Solid 18K Yellow Gold.
Case Diameter: 33mm (excluding crown).
Lug to lug: 37mm
Case Thickness: 6mm.
Crystal: Sapphire Crystal.
Bracelet/Strap: Original Omega Strap with Original Omega Buckle.
Water Resistance: Waterproof Untested. As with all vintage watches, water resistance cannot be guaranteed.

CONDITION
Overall Condition: Good to Very Good Vintage Condition.
The 18K solid gold case remains in good to very good vintage condition, showing only light signs of careful ownership consistent with its age. The original dial is clean and well preserved, while the sapphire crystal provides excellent clarity.
The watch is fitted with its original Omega strap, and all components remain original. The strap and hardware present in good to very good condition, complementing the elegant appearance of this classic Constellation. The Swiss quartz movement has been tested and is operating properly at the time of listing.

COLLECTOR'S NOTE
Introduced in 1982, the Constellation Manhattan represented one of Omega's most significant design evolutions. Created by renowned designer Carol Didisheim, the Manhattan introduced the now-iconic integrated case and bracelet architecture along with the distinctive bezel claws, elements that continue to define the Constellation collection today.

The Ref. 196.1070 elevates this design through its solid 18K yellow gold construction and practical Day-Date complication. Its remarkably slim 6mm profile reflects Omega's mastery of quartz watchmaking during the era, delivering both elegance and exceptional wearing comfort.

Today, solid gold Manhattan references are increasingly sought after by collectors for their timeless design, luxurious materials, and historical importance within the evolution of Omega's flagship dress watch collection.

TERMS OF SALE
This is a genuine vintage Omega timepiece and may exhibit light signs of previous ownership consistent with its age. Please review all photographs carefully, as they form an important part of the item's description. We are happy to provide additional photographs or answer any questions prior to purchase to ensure complete confidence in your selection.

listing.title: Omega constellation manhattan "swiss made omega” special edition 50 years
listing.body:
Vintage Omega Constellation Automatic Chronometer “Manhattan” – Two-Tone Gold & Steel – Diamond Dial – 50 Years Edition

Elegant, timeless, and unmistakably Omega — this vintage Omega Constellation “Manhattan” is a refined luxury watch from the late 1980s to early 1990s, featuring a rare combination of automatic chronometer movement, diamond hour markers, and a commemorative 50 Years caseback.

Crafted in stainless steel with solid 18k yellow gold accents, this watch showcases the iconic Constellation design with its signature “griffes” (claws) and Roman numeral bezel. The integrated bracelet and slim profile make it both comfortable and sophisticated, perfect for daily wear or formal occasions.

The dial is finished in a champagne/silver tone with Omega’s subtle monogram pattern, enhanced by diamond-set hour markers and a date window at 3 o’clock. Powered by a Swiss automatic chronometer-certified movement, this watch represents Omega’s legacy of precision and craftsmanship.

Key Features:
- Brand: Omega  
- Model: Constellation “Manhattan”  
- Movement: Automatic (self-winding), chronometer-certified  
- Case Material: Stainless steel with 18k yellow gold bezel and accents  
- Bracelet: Integrated two-tone steel & gold bracelet  
- Dial: Champagne/silver with diamond hour markers  
- Bezel: Solid gold with engraved Roman numerals  
- Crystal: Sapphire  
- Functions: Hours, minutes, seconds, date  
- Case Size: Approx. 34–36 mm  

Special Details:
- Rare “Constellation 50 Years” commemorative caseback  
- Iconic observatory medallion engraving  
- Classic two-tone luxury aesthetic from Omega’s golden era  

Condition:
Pre-owned vintage condition with light signs of wear consistent with age. The watch is in good working order. (Service history unknown unless otherwise stated.)

Why You’ll Love It:
This is a true vintage Omega with enduring style — combining Swiss mechanical precision, iconic 1980s/90s design, and collectible appeal. A perfect choice for collectors or anyone seeking a distinctive, elegant timepiece.

Feel free to message with any questions or for additional photos.

listing.title: Vintage Omega Constellation Ref 168.016 14K Gold Cap Linen Dial Cal 751 Day Date Chronometer Watch
listing.body:
Authentic Vintage Omega Constellation Ref. CD 168.016 – Automatic Chronometer Caliber 751

This elegant vintage Omega Constellation comes from my personal collection and is now being offered for sale because it is no longer being worn.

The watch features a beautifully textured silver linen-style dial, applied gold-tone and black baton hour markers, and a practical day-date display positioned at 3 o’clock. Its classic 14K gold-capped case gives the watch a refined two-tone appearance while retaining the durability of a stainless steel case back.

At its heart is the respected Omega Caliber 751 automatic chronometer movement. The movement is visually clean and well presented, and the day-date mechanism changes correctly at the time of listing.

WATCH DETAILS

• Brand: Omega
• Collection: Constellation
• Reference: CD 168.016
• Movement: Automatic Omega Caliber 751
• Movement serial number: 27,281,998
• Certification: Officially Certified Chronometer
• Functions: Hours, minutes, seconds, day and date
• Case: 14K gold-capped case with stainless steel case back
• Case diameter: Approximately 35mm, excluding the crown
• Dial: Silver linen-textured dial
• Hour markers: Applied gold-tone and black baton indexes
• Day-date display: Positioned at 3 o’clock
• Crown: Signed Omega crown
• Crystal: Acrylic crystal
• Strap: Newly replaced brown leather strap
• Buckle: New replacement buckle
• Case back: Constellation observatory medallion
• Condition: Attractive vintage condition with normal signs of age and previous use

CONDITION

The silver linen-textured dial remains attractive and provides a distinctive appearance under different lighting. The gold-capped case retains its elegant shape, while the automatic movement appears clean and well preserved.

Please carefully review all photographs, as they are an important part of the condition description. Vintage watches may show small scratches, marks, aging or other signs of previous use.

The watch is currently running and the day-date functions are operating at the time of listing. However, because this is a vintage mechanical watch, daily accuracy and power reserve may vary depending on use.

AUTHENTICITY GUARANTEE

This is an authentic vintage Omega watch. The buyer is welcome to have it inspected and authenticated by any reputable watchmaker, professional watch dealer or independent authentication service.

We fully support professional inspection. Please contact us before allowing the watch to be opened during the return period.

VINTAGE WATCH NOTICE

Water resistance has not been tested and is not guaranteed. Please keep the watch away from water, moisture, steam and other liquids.

RETURN POLICY

Returns are accepted within 14 days from the confirmed delivery date.

The watch must be returned in the same condition in which it was received. No components may be removed, replaced, altered, polished or damaged. A professional authenticity inspection is welcome, but the seller must be informed before the case is opened.

This is a beautiful vintage Omega Constellation suitable for collectors, formal wear or anyone who appreciates classic Swiss chronometer watches.

listing.title: Dive watch "Amphibian" "Wostok", Soviet watch , Men watch Mechanical watch
listing.body:
Vintage diving watch "Wostok" "Amphibian" mechanical watch serviced by a master and works good.

All parts are original.

Stainless steel watch in very good condition - see on photos.

Made in 1970s in USSR for the NAVY.

Amfibia (often spelled "Amphibia" or "Amphibian") is a Soviet watch that in the West would be called a Dive watch. Produced in large quantities for the Soviet and Russian military, these watches gained significant popularity worldwide. The Vostok watch factory created the first Soviet Amphibia watch in 1967. Around the same time, Raketa also started producing a diving watch. Poljot followed with their own version in 1972.

More info here - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amfibia

Specifications:
- waterproof - 200m (not guaranteed)
- shockproof 
- stainless steel case
- revolving bezel
- measures 1,3 inches (3,3 cm) dial in diameter,
 height -1,9''(4,8cm), width with crown-1,7''(4.3cm), thickness 0.43''(1,1cm)
- 18 ruby jewels movement
- hands and dots on the dial are glowing in the dark
- Comes with new leather strap.

Wind-up watch Instruction (Key is needed to loosen and pull up to half and then wind on a maximum (once to wind = 36 hours of work watch)
To transfer the hands - you must pull the key on maximum and transfer the hands.)

Please note:
-All photos are real!!
-Your order will be packaged carefully to ensure it gets to you in perfect condition.
-All vintage items sold in As-Is condition.
-Real colors may slightly differ from their appearance on your display.
-The watch will be carefully packed and shipped within 3 days after payment is received. Ships via Registered Air Mail.

listing.body:
AUTHENTIC VINTAGE OMEGA CONSTELLATION REF. 168.005 – AUTOMATIC CALIBER 561

This elegant vintage Omega Constellation comes from my personal watch collection. I am offering it for sale because it is no longer being worn.

The watch features a classic silver-toned sunburst dome dial, applied yellow-gold-tone baton hour markers with black inserts, a framed date window at 3 o’clock, and the distinctive angular dog-leg lugs associated with this vintage Constellation design.

The warm 14K yellow-gold-capped case is paired with a stainless steel case back featuring the iconic Omega Constellation observatory medallion.

WATCH DETAILS

• Brand: Omega
• Collection: Constellation
• Reference: 168.005
• Movement: Omega automatic Caliber 561
• Movement serial number: 21,434,354
• Jewels: 24 jewels
• Certification: Officially Certified Chronometer
• Case: 14K yellow-gold-capped case with stainless steel case back
• Dial: Silver-toned sunburst dome dial
• Hour markers: Applied gold-tone baton indexes with black inserts
• Hands: Gold-tone hour, minute and central seconds hands
• Date display: Framed date window at 3 o’clock
• Crown: Original signed Omega crown
• Crystal: Acrylic crystal
• Lugs: Classic angular dog-leg lugs
• Case back: Stainless steel with gold Constellation observatory medallion
• Strap: Black leather strap shown in the photographs
• Operation: Running and keeping good time at the time of listing

CONDITION

The yellow-gold-capped case retains attractive and well-defined edges, particularly around the angular lugs.

The silver-toned dial has a subtle sunburst finish that changes beautifully under different lighting. The applied gold-tone indexes with black inserts provide an elegant contrast and excellent readability.

The Omega Caliber 561 automatic chronometer movement appears clean and is running properly at the time of listing.

Please carefully review all photographs, as they show the actual watch being offered and form an important part of the condition description.

As an authentic vintage timepiece, the watch may show light scratches, marks, patina and other signs of previous ownership.

AUTHENTICITY GUARANTEE

This is an authentic vintage Omega watch.

The buyer is welcome to have the watch inspected and authenticated by an Omega-authorized service center, a qualified watchmaker, a reputable vintage watch dealer, or any trusted independent authentication service.

Professional inspection is fully welcomed. Any opening of the watch during the return period must be performed carefully by a qualified professional without altering or damaging the watch.

VINTAGE WATCH NOTICE

Water resistance has not been tested and is not guaranteed.

Please keep the watch away from water, moisture, steam and other liquids. Daily accuracy and power reserve may vary because this is a vintage mechanical watch.

RETURN POLICY

Returns are accepted within 14 days from the confirmed delivery date.

The watch must be returned in the same condition in which it was received. It must not be polished, serviced, damaged, modified, or have any original components removed or replaced.

The buyer may inspect and authenticate the watch at any reputable professional establishment before deciding whether to keep it.

A refined vintage Omega Constellation combining an automatic chronometer movement, classic dog-leg lugs and an elegant yellow-gold-capped case.

I personally serviced this caliber 564, 24 jewel rotor automatic, Officially Certified Chronometer, adjusted 5 positions and it is running strong and keeping time well. Quick set date @ 3 changes smoothly. Serial number 27203012 dates watch to 1968. These photos are of the actual movement in this watch! New Swiss made optical grade acrylic crystal, new gasket and new signed Omega crown. New OmegaAddict high-quality 19 mm black, dark brown or light brown comfortable leather alligator print strap with GOLD buckle.  Please specify choice of color when you make your purchase. Because of their excellent reputation, I can offer a one-year warranty; no charge for labor, only charging for parts (if needed) and return shipping ($20 in U.S. /$45 outside U.S.). 
*FREE LIFETIME SERVICE AGREEMENT:  Your watch should be SERVICED every 3 years after date of purchase.  A SERVICE includes - movement dismantled, movement cleaned and oiled, case cleaned and new crystal.  With this agreement, your 3-Year Service will cost $300 plus parts and return shipping (20 in U.S. /45 outside U.S.).

OmegaAddict - Sales and Service of Vintage Omega Watches
For restoration or service of your VINTAGE OMEGA WATCH message Tim Mackrain. Any problems with a watch purchased from me, I will take care of it right away – always have and always will.  I believe in quality not quantity. Every watch I sell gets my full attention to detail.  Authenticity is money back guaranteed on all my watches. I do not sell fake watches!  We are located in sunny Phoenix, Arizona. Feel free to message me with any watch questions from 8am to 5pm - AZ time. 602-795-8894

listing.title: The Submarine Commanders' Wristwatch, United Kingdom 1931
listing.body:
Rare and Historical ** The Submarine Commanders' Wristwatch, UK 1931 **

Grandfather of the waterproof wristwatch and Godfather of the now iconic Rolex Oyster Submariner, the Submarine Commanders’ wristwatch led the way for Rolex founder Hans Wilsdorf… and ultimately – on March 31st 1922 (copyright N° 51632) - saw its brand-name become one of Rolex’s! 

In the Midst of World War I, two British Submarine Commanders approached Brook & Son requesting they “Consider the construction of a special watch suitable for their work. As Edinburgh's foremost jewelers, watch and clock makers as well as official Goldsmiths to His Majesty The King… to Her Royal Highness Princess Louise… and to The King's Bodyguard (The Royal Company of Archers), this venerable firm accepted the challenge!

The Submariners explained that the watch must fulfill rigorous conditions, notably be water-tight: “For,- even when a submarine is on the surface, the deck is always more-or-less-awash”…  It must be non-magnetic: “For underwater the submarine is driven by electricity and in such a limited space watches made of magnetic materials are necessarily affected”…. Also for the latter reason, use of a compensation balance of the ordinary kind to regulate the watch’s speed would be impossible: “The balance must be of some material which shows a minimum of expansion and contraction due to temperature variations”!

Brook & Son responded with a very innovative solution: 

In designing their water-tight watch case, they correctly understood that any watch’s Achilles heel was the opening through which protrudes the stem with which a watch is set and wound. So, they incorporated a gland-seal in the stem’s passageway, a design innovation that not long thereafter also was incorporated into the Rolex Oyster water-proof screw-down crown, whose patent Rolex founder, Hans Wilsdorf, purchased from George Perret and Paul Perregaux in 1926.

For the Submarine Wrist Watch’s mechanism, Brook & Son turned to Swiss watch-industry giant Tavannes, noted for their very high quality watch movements as well as other cutting-edge watch-making inventions. Tavannes’ solution for the Submarine Wrist Watch was to develop exclusive iron nickel alloy components which not only were impervious to magnetism but also displayed negligible expansion/contraction due to temperature changes.

The Submarine Wristwatch was so ground-breaking that its creation resulted in a scientific publication about it in “The Horological Journal”, December 1917 (see http://www.vintagewatchstraps.com/waterproof.html).

Manufacturing and development of the Submarine Wrist Watch continued well beyond WWI. In 1931, London jeweler and inventor of the expansion bracelet, E. Harrup (in collaboration with F. Wachter in New York) redesigned the Submarine’s case, integrating further improvements (patent N° 358370 and N° 362229), which notably included the bezel and a water-tight snap-back for the case.

A well-documented fact is Rolex’s decades-long preoccupation with producing a water-proof wristwatch. Notably, as of the 1910s, they successively( as well as simultaneously) employed Denison’s screw-back cases, Borgel’s water-tight watchcases, Baumgartner’s double  hermetic cases, etc. for their Rolex watches)… culminating in Rolex’s 1926 launch of the Oyster watchcase. 

Back then, Rolex and the Submarine Wrist Watch both were British watch companies; and Rolex founder Hans Wilsdorf would have followed the development and evolution of this “water-tight watch” competitor, the Submarine Wrist Watch. This is confirmed by Rolex’s 1922 registration of “The Submarine” brand name. Apparently, it wasn’t previously copyrighted. Notwithstanding, almost a decade onward, Harrup still was commercializing wristwatches called “Submarine”!

Interestingly, although the Submarine Wrist Watch also appears to have played a role in Rolex history, including inspiring the name of Rolex’s current line of Sports Watches (the Rolex Submariner), information about the Submarine Wrist Watch, has largely remained a “well-kept secret”…

Indeed, the author of a research publication about the Submarine Wrist Watch, appearing May/June 2014 in the NAWCC Watch & Clock Bulletin, concludes: 

“The one question that puzzles me is why so little is known about these historically important watches? I have never seen them mentioned in any book or article. They were clearly fully waterproof nearly ten years before the Rolex Oyster, which many people think of as the first waterproof watch, or the first waterproof wristwatch. They were also non-magnetic and temperature compensated, if the article in the H[orological] J[ournal] is correct.

The Submarine watch was also very practical compared to the Oyster - there is no need to unscrew the crown to wind or set the watch, and therefore no threads on the stem tube to wear, the Achilles heel of the early Oysters before automatic winding was introduced, they remain waterproof while both winding and setting the watch, which the Oyster doesn't, and there is no need to remember to screw down the crown after winding, a feature that has caused grief to many Oyster owners over the years. The compressed gasket sealing for the stem is perhaps not as ultimately waterproof as a screw down crown in withstanding water pressure at diving depths, but then again, Rolex didn't make any claims about this for the first Oysters, allowing Omega to make the claim of producing the first dive watch in the 1932 Omega Marine.

I suppose the answer could be found in the way the watch came about, during the depths of WW1 as the result of a request by two submarine commanders. The extra work involved in making the watch waterproof and anti-magnetic would have made it more expensive, and the military involvement could have made it hush-hush. Was it regarded as too expensive to be commercially viable, was it secret, or was it that no one involved saw that the public might want a waterproof watch - 1917 was of course long before recreational diving became popular, or was even possible. The promotion of a waterproof watch as something for the average person to want or need seems to have been a particular vision of Hans Wilsdorf, similar to the way that Steve Jobs had a vision for the iPod and iPad and almost single handedly created markets for portable mp3 players and tablet computers. But without such a visionary to champion its cause this watch faded into obscurity.”

Watchcase: 9K Solid Gold… With fluted bezel (visually identical to 1st generation Rolex Oysters, as is the form, size and appearance overall). Signed on case back SUBMARINE, LONDON MADE, PAT. APP. FOR

Hallmarks: London, 375 and 9 Hallmarks (9K Solid Gold). Date-Mark 1931. Goldsmith's Mark: EH (for E.G. Harrup)

Dimensions 30 mm (excluding the winding crown) x 40 mm (lug-to-lug)

Dial: Porcelain enamel, 24 Hour (1 - 11 Black Numerals and 12 - 24 Red Numerals)

Bracelet: New-Old-Stock Hand-Stiched leather band, manufactured in the same time-period as the watch

Condition: Excellent, Serviced and tested by our Master Swiss Watchmaker

N.B.: The Submarine Watch was designed to be “water-tight” (i.e., humidity and moisture resistant); it is early vintage and should not be immersed!

listing.title: Vintage Universal Genève Automatic Watch Cal 138SS 14K Solid Gold Case Sharp & Dohme Dial 1954 Presentation Watch Running
listing.body:
I placed on a time graph and it’s running +- 30 seconds a day 

This elegant mid-century Swiss wristwatch represents a fascinating intersection of fine horology and American pharmaceutical history. Produced by the prestigious Swiss manufacturer Universal Genève, the watch houses the respected Caliber 138SS automatic movement, one of the brand’s early self-winding calibers developed during the golden era of mechanical watchmaking in the late 1940s and 1950s. Universal Genève was widely admired for its refined engineering and reliable in-house movements, and the Caliber 138 series became one of the company’s dependable automatic platforms during the post-war expansion of Swiss wristwatch production.

The watch is housed in a solid 14K gold case manufactured by the Star Watch Case Company of Taunton, Massachusetts, a respected American case maker that produced high-quality gold cases for imported Swiss movements destined for the United States market. With gold prices historically strong, the case itself carries substantial intrinsic value while maintaining the classic understated luxury expected of a mid-century Swiss dress watch.

The dial is marked “Sharp & Dohme – Automatic – Swiss,” referencing the historic American pharmaceutical company Sharp & Dohme. Founded in the 19th century and later merged with Merck & Co., the company frequently commissioned fine Swiss watches as presentation awards for executives and high-performing employees. Watches such as this were commonly given in recognition of professional achievement or years of service.

The back of the case remains engraved with its original presentation inscription:

D.G. CLEMMONS
MEMBER – 1954
ALL AMERICAN SALES TEAM

This engraving firmly dates the watch to the early 1950s and connects the piece to its original owner and the mid-century corporate culture in which presentation watches were symbols of recognition and accomplishment.

The watch is currently fitted with a MOD DEP Swiss-made rubber strap, a comfortable vintage strap style that wears well while helping protect the original gold case.

This example has clearly been cared for over its lifetime and the movement shows signs of past servicing. The watch will run and keep time when manually wound and left resting, and it has been worn throughout the week with reasonable timekeeping. However, when the crown is pulled out to set the time, the hands tend to stick or hesitate during adjustment. Because of this behavior, the watch should be professionally serviced in order to run properly and ensure smooth operation of the time-setting mechanism. As with most mechanical watches from the 1950s, routine servicing is considered normal maintenance and will help preserve the movement for continued use.

Altogether this piece represents a wonderful example of mid-century Swiss watchmaking, combining Universal Genève engineering, a solid 14K gold case, and a unique connection to American pharmaceutical corporate history.

listing.title: Jonah Automatic Dive Watch
listing.body:
Jonah Diver — White Dial & Blue Bezel Automatic Watch

GRACE REACHES DEEPER THAN THE SEA

The Jonah Diver is a faith-inspired automatic watch created as a reminder that no failure, distance, or darkness can place us beyond the reach of God’s grace.

Jonah ran from God’s calling and found himself in the depths of the sea. Yet even there, God heard his prayer, preserved his life, and gave him another opportunity to obey.

Jonah 2:9 declares:

“Salvation belongs to the Lord.”

The Jonah Diver was created for those who have experienced second chances—and for anyone who needs the reminder that God’s grace does not stop at the shoreline. It reaches into the depths.

A BRIGHTER NAUTICAL DESIGN

This version of the Jonah Diver pairs a clean white dial with a light-blue 60-minute bezel and a distinctive orange seconds hand. The bright nautical colorway gives the watch a crisp, energetic character while preserving the purposeful design of the Jonah collection.

The dial bears the words “From the Depths,” connecting the watch to Jonah’s prayer and the truth that God hears us even in our lowest moments.

Its luminous hands and hour markers provide strong visibility in low light. Inside is the dependable Japanese NH35 automatic movement, visible through the exhibition caseback. A custom rotor engraved with Galatians 4:4 connects the watch to the verse that inspired the Fullness of Time name.

WATCH SPECIFICATIONS

Movement: Japanese NH35 automatic
Case: 40mm stainless steel
Caseback: Exhibition caseback
Rotor: Custom Galatians 4:4 rotor
Crystal: Sapphire
Dial: White
Bezel: Light-blue 60-minute bezel
Seconds hand: Orange
Bracelet: Stainless steel
Functions: Hours, minutes, seconds, and date
Illumination: Luminous hands, hour markers, and bezel pip
Water resistance: Individually pressure tested to 5 ATM
Assembly: Hand assembled and tested in the USA

Weight - 5.453 oz

INDIVIDUALLY TESTED

Every Jonah Diver is individually inspected, evaluated for accuracy on a timegrapher, and pressure tested to 5 ATM.

The specific rate, amplitude, beat error, and pressure-test result for this watch are recorded on its accompanying Certificate of Stewardship.

As with all mechanical watches, daily accuracy can vary depending on wearing habits, position, temperature, and winding state.

THE EXACT WATCH PICTURED

The watch shown in these photographs is the actual watch you will receive—not a stock photograph or representative example.

A HAND-FINISHED TIMEPIECE

Each dial is hand finished using custom lettering created in-house. Because of this handmade process, minor edging from the dial application may be visible in certain lighting or under magnification. During normal wear and in natural lighting, these details are subtle and contribute to the individual character of a hand-finished timepiece.

PRESENTED WITH PURPOSE

Your Jonah Diver arrives with:

• Presentation watch box
• Certificate of Stewardship
• Individually documented timegrapher results
• Individually documented pressure-test result

ABOUT FULLNESS OF TIME

Fullness of Time Watch Company is a small Christian-owned watch brand created to share faith, encourage meaningful conversations, and point people to Jesus Christ.

Time is one of God’s greatest gifts. We pray this watch serves as a reminder to invest your days wisely, love generously, and walk faithfully.

A watch tells you what time it is. Your calling tells you what to do with it.

listing.title: c. 1963 Vintage Zodiac Sea Wolf Ref. 699 Automatic 17-Jewel Swiss Dive Watch – Working
listing.body:
Excellent original vintage Zodiac Sea Wolf automatic dive watch, dating to approximately c. 1963 and representing one of the early generations of Zodiac’s now-iconic Sea Wolf. This desirable no-date example features the classic silver/off-white dial with applied hour markers and distinctive luminous triangular markers containing Arabic numerals at 3, 6, 9 and 12 o’clock. The dial is signed Zodiac Sea Wolf, Automatic and Swiss T<25, accompanied by the characteristic black dauphine-style luminous hands and sweep seconds hand.

Introduced during the formative years of the modern recreational dive watch, the Zodiac Sea Wolf became one of the company’s most recognizable sports watches and developed a particularly strong following during the 1960s. Early examples such as this used a compact stainless steel case, rotating metal timing bezel and 17-jewel Swiss automatic movement. The Sea Wolf was also notably popular among American servicemen during the Vietnam era, contributing to the model’s enduring reputation among military and vintage dive-watch collectors.

The watch retains considerable vintage character. The original-style silver dial has developed an attractive aged patina, while the stainless steel case and rotating bezel show honest surface wear and scratches from decades of use. Fitted with a vintage stainless steel adjustable bracelet with folding clasp.
